metadata.summary: A day after world No 1 Elena Rybakina was knocked out of the China Open, world No 2 Aryna Sabalenka followed suit in Beijing on Sunday.
metadata.content: China Open: Aryna Sabalenka suffers shock Beijing exit — a day after new world No 1 Elena Rybakina was knocked out | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content China Open: Aryna Sabalenka suffers shock Beijing exit — a day after new world No 1 Elena Rybakina was knocked out Aryna Sabalenka exits the Beijing tournament in straight sets against Czech teenager Nikola Bartunkova, while Carlos Alcaraz advances in Tokyo; you can watch the WTA/ATP China Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports Sunday 4 October 2026 08:30, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Nikola Bartunkova against Aryna Sabalenka from the China Open A day after world No 1 Elena Rybakina was knocked out of the China Open, world No 2 Aryna Sabalenka followed suit in Beijing on Sunday. Czech 20-year-old Nikola Bartunkova defeated the four-time Grand Slam champion 6-4 6-3, leaving the tournament without its two top seeds in the opening week. Rybakina was knocked out on Saturday, and Sabalenka has now joined her in an early exit from the WTA 1000 event in Beijing. messages.text: Humphries to face Price in World Grand Prix final in 2023 repeat

metadata.summary: Gerwyn Price and Luke Humphries will look for their second World Grand Prix titles when they meet in Sunday's final of the double-start event in Leicester.
metadata.content: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries to face Gerywn Price in Sunday's final in Leicester, live on Sky Sports | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries to face Gerywn Price in Sunday's final in Leicester, live on Sky Sports Luke Humphries reaches fourth straight World Grand Prix final after beating two-time champion James Wade in semis; Gerwyn Price defeats Nathan Aspinall as he targets first major title since 2022; watch live on Sky Sports+ and Sky Sports Main Event from 8pm Sunday Sunday 4 October 2026 01:38, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Humphries was delighted to make a record-breaking fourth consecutive World Grand Prix final after playing 'consistent' darts against James Wade Gerwyn Price and Luke Humphries will look for their second World Grand Prix titles when they meet in Sunday's final of the double-start event in Leicester. Price, the 2020 champion, beat Nathan Aspinall 5-2 in Saturday's first semi-final before 2023 winner Luke Humphries defeated James Wade 5-3 to reach his fourth straight final and set up a repeat of the showpiece game three years ago - when he saw off Price 5-2. A major drought will end either way at the Mattioli Arena, with Humphries going over a year since his last premier title - the 2025 Premier League - and Price's previous elite silverware coming way back in 2022 at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam. messages.text: Humphries: Reaching final 'doesn't mean anything' without beating Price!

metadata.summary: Luke Humphries insists reaching a record-breaking fourth consecutive World Grand Prix final will count for nothing if he doesn’t beat Gerwyn Price to the title in Leicester.
metadata.content: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries says reaching final 'doesn't mean anything' without beating Gerwyn Price to title | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries says reaching final 'doesn't mean anything' without beating Gerwyn Price to title Luke Humphries and Gerwyn Price will meet in Sunday’s World Grand Prix final; Humphries beat Price to the 2023 title but has been runner-up in the last two years at the Mattioli Arena; watch live from 8pm on Sky Sports Main Event Sunday 4 October 2026 07:38, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Humphries was delighted to make a record-breaking fourth consecutive World Grand Prix final and said he managed to produce 'controlled and consistent' darts Luke Humphries insists reaching a record-breaking fourth consecutive World Grand Prix final will count for nothing if he doesn’t beat Gerwyn Price to the title in Leicester. Humphries made history by becoming the first player to reach the final in four consecutive years at the double-in event, defeating James Wade 5-3 to book his place in Sunday's showpiece at the Mattioli Arena. 'Cool Hand' was runner-up to Luke Littler after a 6-1 thrashing last year and suffered a shock 6-4 loss to Mike de Decker in 2024, with Humphries now hoping for a repeat of his 2023 victory over Price when the two former world champions meet again at the final. messages.text: 'Complete' England display reinvigorates faith in Tuchel project - for now

metadata.summary: "We will always have a scar, we will always feel pain and disappointment. But this is the way to move forward."
metadata.content: Croatia 0-7 England: Thumping win reinvigorates Thomas Tuchel's project after World Cup blow - but next Spain test will define progress towards success | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Croatia 0-7 England: Thumping win reinvigorates Thomas Tuchel's project after World Cup blow - but next Spain test will define progress towards success England's attack was electric and devastating in huge Nations League win in Croatia; performance best of Thomas Tuchel era and highlights areas of progress; but after World Cup heartache England's prospects of future success on big stage will be judged by Spain away in November Peter Smith Senior Football Journalist @psmithXI Sunday 4 October 2026 07:15, UK Image: Harry Kane slides in England's fifth goal against Croatia "We will always have a scar, we will always feel pain and disappointment. But this is the way to move forward." Thomas Tuchel knows England's frustrating, much-criticised semi-final defeat to Argentina at the World Cup will hang over him and his team right through until the Euros in 2028 - and even beyond. But in Croatia on Saturday, a thumping 7-0 win was a performance and result to reinvigorate Tuchel's England project. It was a historic scoreline: Croatia's heaviest defeat. No team had scored more than four goals away to them before. metadata.summary: Lachlan Walmsley is potentially in the most unique position of all. A Super League Grand Final winner with Wakefield Trinity and without a contract for 2027.
metadata.content: The Super League Grand Final winner without a contract for 2027: Wakefield Trinity's Lachlan Walmsley lives out dream but uncertainty lies ahead | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content The Super League Grand Final winner without a contract for 2027: Wakefield Trinity's Lachlan Walmsley lives out dream but uncertainty lies ahead Lachlan Walmsley came up with an assist in the Super League Grand Final but is without a contract for 2027; he was part of the Wakefield side that made history and ended a 58-year top-flight trophy drought Megan Wellens Sports Journalist @MegWellensX Saturday 3 October 2026 23:27, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League Grand Final between Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity Lachlan Walmsley is potentially in the most unique position of all. A Super League Grand Final winner with Wakefield Trinity and without a contract for 2027. Walmsley was part of the Wakefield side that made history with their 23-10 victory over Warrington Wolves in the Super League Grand Final to become only the sixth winners of the competition. It ended a 58-year top-flight trophy drought for a side that have gone through everything Super League has had to offer. From at one point struggling to keep the lights on, they are now at the top of the sport. Wakefield beat Warrington to claim historic Grand Final win Super League Grand Final 2026: As it happened!
